llm_analysis.title: DT-TacVLA: A Dual-Timescale Tactile-Enhanced Vision-Language-Action Model for Contact-Rich Manipulation
llm_analysis.takeaway: DT-TacVLA targets contact-rich manipulation, where vision-centric VLA perception struggles to capture contact establishment, in-hand slip, and normal and shear contact interactions. Built on SmolVLA, it adds a dual-timescale tactile fusion framework: a slow semantic pathway that fuses tactile image sequences with VLM features through semantic-guided gating to produce a task-contact context, and a fast reflex pathway that encodes tactile marker displacements into tokens injected into the action expert via a Tactile-Marker Adapter. Across power plug insertion, USB connector insertion, and test tube placement, the abstract reports consistently higher success rates than vision-only VLA baselines and ablation variants. Inspect how the slow context is reused across fast reflex updates and how the adapter modulates action chunks.

llm_analysis.title: X2-N: A Transformable Wheel-Legged Humanoid Robot With Dual-Mode Locomotion and Manipulation
llm_analysis.takeaway: X2-N addresses the reduced legged stability of fixed-wheel feet and limited hip degrees of freedom in wheel-legged robots, plus the absence of a full upper body for dexterous manipulation. The proposed high-DoF transformable robot operates in humanoid and wheel-legged forms and transforms between them through joint reconfiguration, with a reinforcement learning-based whole-body control framework tailored to this morphology for hybrid locomotion, transformation, and manipulation. The abstract reports validation on dynamic skating-like motion, stair climbing, and package delivery, but its results sentence is truncated, so no specific metrics are available. Inspect the joint-reconfiguration mechanism and how one control framework spans the hybrid modes.

llm_analysis.title: EMMA: Scaling Mobile Manipulation via Egocentric Human Data
llm_analysis.takeaway: EMMA tackles the bottleneck of expensive mobile robot teleoperation for scaling mobile manipulation imitation learning by training policies from human mobile manipulation data together with static robot data, sidestepping mobile teleoperation. The framework co-trains human full-body motion data with static robot data end-to-end. Across four real-world tasks, the abstract reports comparable performance to baselines trained on teleoperated mobile robot data (Mobile ALOHA), with higher or equivalent full task success, generalization to new spatial configurations and scenes, and positive performance scaling as hours of human data increase. Inspect how the human and static robot data are combined and what the scaling observation covers.

llm_analysis.title: Crossing the Reality Gap: A Survey on Sim-to-Real Transferability of Robot Controllers in Reinforcement Learning
llm_analysis.takeaway: This survey addresses the reality gap in reinforcement learning for robot control, where approximate simulated dynamics cause simulated and real control-law performance to mismatch and transferred controllers can fail on the real robot. Its stated goals are to identify the main approaches to the reality gap problem in RL-based robot control, point out their shortcomings, and outline new potential research areas. It is useful as a knowledge map for organizing sim-to-real methods and their limitations rather than as a new method. Inspect how the approaches are categorized and which shortcomings the authors attribute to each category.

historical_paper.title: DT-TacVLA: A Dual-Timescale Tactile-Enhanced Vision-Language-Action Model for Contact-Rich Manipulation
historical_paper.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models exhibit strong semantic understanding and policy generalization, yet their predominantly vision-centric perception struggles to characterize key contact states such as contact establishment, in-hand slip, and normal and shear contact interactions. This limits their performance in contact-rich manipulation. In this paper, we proposeDT-TacVLA(Dual-Timescale Tactile-Enhanced VLA), a dual-timescale tactile fusion framework built on top of SmolVLA that processes tactile inputs along two complementary slow and fast pathways. Theslow semantic pathwayoperates at a lower update rate and adaptively fuses tactile image sequences with VLM features through a semantic-guided gating mechanism, producing a task-contact context that can be reused across multiple fast reflex updates. Thefast reflex pathwayis updated multiple times within each slow-context window. Under the fixed slow-context conditioning, it encodes the current tactile marker displacements into compact tokens and injects them into the action expert through a Tactile-Marker Adapter, modulating the action chunk with real-time contact feedback. Across three contact-rich real-world manipulation tasks, including power plug insertion, USB connector insertion, and test tube placement, DT-TacVLA consistently achieves higher success rates than vision-only VLA baselines and its ablation variants.

historical_paper.title: EMMA: Scaling Mobile Manipulation via Egocentric Human Data
historical_paper.abstract: Scaling mobile manipulation imitation learning is bottlenecked by expensive mobile robot teleoperation. We present Egocentric Mobile MAnipulation (EMMA), an end-to-end framework training mobile manipulation policies from human mobile manipulation data with static robot data, sidestepping mobile teleoperation. To accomplish this, we co-train human full-body motion data with static robot data. In our experiments across four real-world tasks, EMMA demonstrates comparable performance to baselines trained on teleoperated mobile robot data (Mobile ALOHA), achieving higher or equivalent task performance in full task success. We find that EMMA is able to generalize to new spatial configurations and scenes, and we observe positive performance scaling as we increase the hours of human data, opening new avenues for scalable robotic learning in real-world environments. Details of this project can be found at:https://ego-moma.github.io

historical_paper.title: Crossing the Reality Gap: A Survey on Sim-to-Real Transferability of Robot Controllers in Reinforcement Learning
historical_paper.abstract: The growing demand for robots able to act autonomously in complex scenarios has widely accelerated the introduction of Reinforcement Learning (RL) in robots control applications. However, the trial and error intrinsic nature of RL may result in long training time on real robots and, moreover, it may lead to dangerous outcomes. While simulators are useful tools to accelerate RL training and to ensure safety, they often are provided only with an approximated model of robot dynamics and of its interaction with the surrounding environment, thus resulting in what is called the reality gap (RG): a mismatch of simulated and real control-law performances caused by the inaccurate representation of the real environment in simulation. The most undesirable result occurs when the controller learnt in simulation fails the task on the real robot, thus resulting in an unsuccessful sim-to-real transfer. The goal of the present survey is threefold: (1) to identify the main approaches to face the RG problem in the context of robot control with RL, (2) to point out their shortcomings, and (3) to outline new potential research areas.
